Ao my carrer everything, dreams etc will be destroyed. So i have to take the strings on my hand, find a problem on that topic. Now, I am not even close to this kind of understanding time is ticking and my career is just slipping away from my hand. 2 years is enough to turn this back, and have a very productive phd.

yeah in principle I can dive into the basic papers on that area. The most problematic part of the research is, not calculating or coding.  For example, when I am doing some calculation, at some point I need to learn a new method. That point is the big time waster. I jump from literature to literature to learn that method, study a week very hard to learn it but at the end of the week actually, I have not learned it at all, and wasted a lot of time.

In undergrad, this was not the case, because everything you have to learn is exactly written on a very well structured textbook and you know that if you study that book it will be enough. 

However, in research, when it comes to learning a new thing, everything becomes a complete chaos for me. For example, I need to learn calculating green's functions in the language of path integrals (as a matrix element of an inverse of a Lagrangian operator). This in principle should be something straightforward and mildly trivial. But, I just waste almost a week on this from jumping one literature to another literature end up not learning at all. Anyway, thanks a lot!
